enonce.question: Write an argumentative essay of about 150 words to support the following statement: 'Social media has a positive impact on society.' Use at least two arguments to justify your point of view.
Name the three parts of the PEE paragraph pattern used in argumentative writing.
Which of these is a strong thesis statement? A) 'Technology is interesting.' B) 'Schools should teach coding because it develops logical thinking and prepares students for future jobs.'
Sort these expressions into OPINION language or CONCESSION language: 'I firmly believe', 'admittedly', 'there is no doubt that', 'it is true that some people'.
Turn this weak thesis into a strong one: 'Reading is good.'
Write a counter-argument and a refutation for the thesis 'Homework should be reduced'. Use a concession linker.

Order these three arguments for the thesis 'Cycling to school is beneficial' from WEAKEST to STRONGEST: (a) it is cheaper than the bus, (b) it keeps students healthy and fit, (c) it saves a little time on short trips.

Write an argumentative essay of about 200 words to argue against the following statement: 'Homework should be abolished in schools.' Use at least two counterarguments to challenge the statement and support your opinion.
Write an introduction (3 sentences) for an argumentative essay on 'Should plastic bottles be banned in schools?' Move from a general hook to a clear thesis.
Write a complete PEE body paragraph (Point, Evidence, Link) defending the idea that 'students should learn a musical instrument'.

Write a full argumentative essay (about 180-220 words) defending ONE clear position on: 'Should students be allowed to use the internet freely during lessons?' Include a thesis, two arguments, a counter-argument with a refutation, and a conclusion.

Read this weak conclusion and rewrite it properly for an argumentative essay whose thesis is that 'volunteering benefits young people': 'So volunteering is good. Also, young people should recycle more and eat healthy food.'

Write an argumentative essay of about 250 words to discuss the following statement: 'Technology in the classroom enhances learning more than traditional teaching methods.' Use at least three arguments to support your view and address a potential counterargument.

Write a full argumentative essay (about 180-220 words) defending ONE clear position on: 'Is it better to read printed books than digital ones?' Support your view with at least two arguments and answer one opposing point.
Match each signal word to its function: (a) therefore (b) although (c) because. Functions: contrast, cause, conclusion.
Read the sentence and decide whether it is a FACT or an OPINION: 'Reading for thirty minutes a day is the best habit a teenager can build.'

Read the following argumentative text and answer the question below.

"Many people argue that social media has a negative impact on teenagers. They claim that it reduces face-to-face communication, increases anxiety, and exposes young people to cyberbullying. However, others believe that social media helps teenagers stay connected with friends, provides educational resources, and allows them to express their creativity. Who is right?"

What is the main argument presented in the text?
In the sentence 'Many people claim that video games are harmful; however, recent studies show they can improve reaction time,' which idea is the writer's own position?
Read: 'Night buses would let workers who finish late return home safely. Yet the city has cut evening routes to save money.' What can you INFER about the writer's opinion of the cuts?

Read the passage and identify the thesis: 'Plastic bags are cheap and convenient, but their cost to nature is enormous. They pollute the sea, harm animals and take centuries to break down. Cloth bags, though slightly more expensive, are a far wiser choice.'
Read: 'Supporters of longer school days say students learn more. Opponents reply that tired minds learn little.' Identify the counter-argument to the idea that longer days help learning.
Find the word in this sentence that shows it is an opinion, not a fact: 'Tourists should certainly visit the ancient ruins before the crowded summer months.'
State the tone (neutral, enthusiastic, critical or worried) of this sentence: 'It is alarming that so many young drivers ignore basic safety rules on our roads.'

Read the following paragraph and answer the questions below.

"The use of plastic bags should be banned in all supermarkets. Plastic bags are harmful to the environment because they take hundreds of years to decompose. They also pollute oceans and harm marine life. Moreover, reusable bags are a better alternative as they are durable and can be used multiple times. Therefore, banning plastic bags is a necessary step to protect our planet."

A) What is the main claim made in the paragraph?
B) Identify two pieces of evidence used to support the claim.

Read the passage and answer A, B and C. 'Fast food is popular among students because it is cheap and quick. However, doctors warn that a diet rich in salt and sugar can lead to serious health problems later in life. Schools could help by offering fresh, affordable meals in their canteens. A small change today may protect a whole generation tomorrow.' A) What is the writer's main claim? B) Give one argument the writer uses to support it. C) Explain the meaning of the last sentence in your own words.

Read the following argumentative text and answer the questions below.

"Some people believe that school uniforms should be mandatory in all public schools. They argue that uniforms reduce bullying based on clothing choices, promote equality among students, and help maintain discipline. On the other hand, opponents claim that uniforms restrict students' freedom of expression, are expensive for low-income families, and do not necessarily improve academic performance. Despite these arguments, the evidence suggests that uniforms have more benefits than drawbacks."

A) Identify the two opposing views on school uniforms.
B) What is the writer's position on the issue?
C) Find one piece of evidence used to support the writer's position.

Read and analyse: 'Cities keep building more roads to fight traffic jams, yet the jams always return. Every new lane simply attracts more cars. Perhaps the real answer lies not in wider roads but in better trains and buses.' A) What problem does the text discuss? B) What does the writer suggest is wrong with the current solution? C) State the writer's purpose in one sentence.

Read: 'Some argue that homework should be abolished, claiming it causes stress. Others insist it builds discipline and reinforces learning. In truth, the problem is not homework itself but its quantity. A few meaningful tasks are far better than a heavy, pointless load.' A) Summarise the two opposing views. B) What solution does the writer propose? C) Does the writer completely support or completely reject homework? Justify with a phrase from the text.
Sort these linkers into ADDING or CONTRASTING: moreover, however, in addition, on the other hand.
Rewrite this informal sentence in a formal, essay style: 'Loads of people think TV is a waste of time.'
Write a for and against essay (about 150 words) on the topic: 'Should students have mobile phones at school?' Use at least two arguments for and two against. Use appropriate linking words.
Put the four parts of a for-and-against essay in the correct order: conclusion, arguments against, introduction, arguments for.
Complete this balanced concluding sentence: 'Having considered both sides, I believe that online learning ...'

Write a for and against essay (about 200 words) on the topic: 'Is social media beneficial or harmful for teenagers?' Use at least three arguments for and three against. Include examples where possible.
For the topic 'Should students wear school uniforms?', write ONE argument FOR and ONE argument AGAINST, each with a short example.
Build a four-block plan (introduction, for, against, conclusion) for the topic 'Should fast food be banned near schools?' Give only the key ideas, not full sentences.
Improve this repetitive passage by replacing the repeated linker: 'However, cars are useful. However, they pollute. However, they cost a lot.'
Write a clear TOPIC SENTENCE to open a paragraph that will present the arguments AGAINST tourism in fragile natural areas.

Write a for and against essay (about 250 words) on the topic: 'Should homework be abolished in schools?' Use at least four arguments for and four against. Support your arguments with logical reasoning and examples.
Write a balanced essay (about 140-170 words) on: 'Should social media be part of the school curriculum?' Use at least four different linking words and underline them in your answer.
Write a full for-and-against essay (about 150-180 words) on: 'Is it better to live in a city or in the countryside?' Keep the body neutral and give your opinion only in the conclusion.

Write a full for-and-against essay (about 150-180 words) on the topic: 'Should teenagers be allowed to have a part-time job during the school year?' Include an introduction, one paragraph FOR, one paragraph AGAINST, and a balanced conclusion.
Fill the gap with 'so': 'The library was closed, ______ we studied at home.'
Choose the correct word: 'The concert was cancelled ______ the storm.' (because / because of)
Label each linker as CAUSE or CONSEQUENCE: since, therefore, due to, as a result.

Complete the sentences with the appropriate cause or consequence linker from the list: because, so, since, therefore, as.
1. She missed the bus _____ she woke up late.
2. The weather was bad; _____, we stayed at home.
3. _____ he studied hard, he passed the exam.
4. _____ it was raining, we took an umbrella.
5. He didn’t eat breakfast; _____, he felt hungry all morning.
Join these two sentences using 'because': 'The exam was difficult. Many students failed it.'
Rewrite using 'due to' + noun phrase: 'The trains were delayed because it snowed heavily.'
Choose the correct linker: 'She studied every evening; ______, she passed with distinction.' (owing to / consequently)

Rewrite the following sentences using the linker in brackets. Make any necessary changes.
1. He didn’t go to school. He was sick. (because of)
2. The traffic was heavy. We arrived late. (as a result)
3. She didn’t study. She failed the test. (so)
4. The movie was boring. We left early. (therefore)
5. He was tired. He went to bed early. (since)
Correct the mistake: 'Because the road was blocked, so we took another way.'
Rewrite this sentence with 'therefore', using correct punctuation: 'The battery was flat, so the phone would not switch on.'

Read the text and fill in the gaps with the appropriate cause or consequence linker from the list: because, so, since, therefore, as a result, consequently, for this reason.
Last weekend, I decided to go hiking in the mountains. _____ the weather was beautiful, I expected a great day out. However, I forgot to bring enough water. _____, I got dehydrated and had to cut my hike short. _____, my friends and I decided to go to a café instead. _____ I hadn’t prepared properly, I wasn’t dressed appropriately for the hike. _____, I caught a cold the next day. I won’t make the same mistake again!

Read and correct all the linker errors in this paragraph: 'Because of the weather was bad, the trip was cancelled. The students were disappointed, therefore they organised an indoor activity instead. Since of the heavy rain, they stayed in the hall.'
Write a short paragraph (4-5 sentences) about pollution in cities. Use at least THREE different cause-and-consequence linkers and underline them.
Combine each pair into one sentence, using a DIFFERENT linker for each: (1) The alarm did not ring. She woke up late. (2) Prices increased. Sales dropped. (3) He trained daily. He improved quickly.
Put the verb in the correct present tense: 'Water ______ (boil) at 100 degrees Celsius.'
Choose 'since' or 'for': 'They have lived in Sfax ______ five years.'
Put the verb in the past simple: 'Yesterday, she ______ (write) a long email.'

Complete the following sentences with the correct form of the verbs in brackets using the present perfect simple or continuous. 
1. She ______ (study) English for three years now. 
2. They ______ (not/see) each other since last summer. 
3. How long ______ you ______ (know) your best friend? 
4. He ______ (work) on this project since January.
Correct the mistake: 'I am wanting a cup of tea right now.'
Use the past perfect: 'When we arrived at the cinema, the film ______ (already/start).'
Choose 'will' or 'be going to': 'Look at those dark clouds! It ______ rain.'
Choose present perfect or past simple: 'She ______ (visit) Rome twice, but she ______ (not go) there last year.'
Present perfect or present perfect continuous? 'She is tired because she ______ (study) all afternoon.'
Complete with the correct tense (past simple or past continuous): 'I ______ (read) a book when the lights ______ (go) out.'

Rewrite the following sentences using the correct form of the verbs in brackets with the past perfect simple or continuous. 
1. By the time we arrived, the film ______ (already/start). 
2. She was tired because she ______ (clean) the house all morning. 
3. They ______ (live) in this city for five years before they moved. 
4. He ______ (wait) for two hours when the bus finally arrived.

Find and correct the FOUR tense mistakes: 'I have went to the library yesterday. I am knowing the librarian for years. While I read, my phone was ringing. I have finished my project since three days.'

Choose the correct option (A, B, or C) to complete each sentence with the appropriate tense (future perfect simple or continuous).
1. By next year, she ______ (teach) for ten years.
   A. will have taught
   B. will have been teaching
   C. will teach
2. They ______ (finish) the project by the time you get here.
   A. will finish
   B. will have finished
   C. will be finishing
3. By the end of this month, he ______ (work) in this company for twenty years.
   A. will work
   B. will have worked
   C. will have been working
4. When you come back, we ______ (decorate) the house for three hours.
   A. will decorate
   B. will have decorated
   C. will have been decorating

Rewrite this paragraph, putting every verb in brackets into the correct tense: 'Last weekend, we (decide) to visit the old medina. While we (walk) through the narrow streets, we (meet) an old friend who (live) there since childhood. We (never see) such a lively market before.'
Write a short paragraph (4-6 sentences) about your day so far. Use at least the present perfect, the past simple and the present continuous, and underline one example of each.
